item.name: Hermes background review fork lifecycle
item.contract: After turns that trigger memory or skill review, Gormes can launch a quiet background review fork that inherits the active runtime credentials, runs only memory and skills toolsets, writes to shared stores without mutating parent history, emits one attributed self-improvement summary, and always cleans up approval callbacks and memory providers
item.degraded_mode: Learning-loop status reports background_review_unavailable, background_review_runtime_unavailable, background_review_denied_toolset, or background_review_cleanup_failed instead of running a full-tool child agent silently.
ready_when: Background review toolset restriction is validated, so the review fork can be memory+skills-only from construction.
Native skills list/view tool surface and Hermes skill_manage support-file and curator intent actions are validated, so the review fork can inspect and mutate skills without a Python subprocess.
Tests can use fake review runners and fake stores; no live provider, Telegram, gateway, or shell command is required.
not_ready_when: The slice grants terminal, browser, file-write outside skill_manage, provider-management, or foreground subagent toolsets to the background fork.
The slice re-resolves credentials from environment variables instead of inheriting the active runtime binding.
The slice mutates parent conversation history or re-surfaces stale tool messages from the inherited transcript as new review actions.
blocked_by: Hermes skill_manage support-file and curator intent actions
unblocks: Hermes curator state transitions and run reports
acceptance: TestBackgroundReviewFork_InheritsActiveRuntime proves provider, model, api_mode, base_url, api_key, credential pool, platform, parent_session_id, and memory store flags are copied from the active parent into the fake review worker.

TestBackgroundReviewFork_RestrictsTools proves the worker receives only memory and skills toolsets and denies terminal, browser, execute_code, network, file_write, and provider-management toolsets with background_review_toolset evidence.
TestBackgroundReviewFork_SkipsPriorToolMessages proves summaries ignore tool messages already present in the inherited transcript and only report successful review-tool actions from the fork.
TestBackgroundReviewFork_EmitsAttributedSummary proves CLI/gateway callbacks receive exactly one `Self-improvement review` summary when memory or skills were updated.
TestBackgroundReviewFork_Cleanup proves approval callbacks are auto-deny during the run, cleared after the run, and memory providers are shutdown before close.
item.note: Hermes v0.12.0 made the after-turn self-improvement review concrete: it forks an AIAgent with the active runtime binding, memory+skills toolsets, auto-deny approvals, parent session attribution, prompt-history isolation, and explicit `Self-improvement review` user-facing summaries. Gormes already has the toolset-restriction policy; this row wires the lifecycle without adding curator scheduling yet. Completed 2026-05-06 with RED evidence from `go test ./internal/hermes -run TestBackgroundReviewFork -count=1` failing on missing background review lifecycle types, then GREEN evidence from the focused Hermes slice and the row package commands.
done_signal: Background review fixtures prove runtime inheritance, memory+skills-only tools, prompt-history isolation, attributed summaries, auto-deny approval behavior, and cleanup without live model calls.

provenance.note: Hermes owns the background review lifecycle contract; Gormes ports it through Go-native review runners and existing memory/skills tool surfaces.

item.name: Hermes review prompt transient-environment guard
item.contract: Gormes' native curator review prompt must preserve Hermes' current class-first learning guard: background review may capture durable reusable fixes, but must not create or harden skills from transient setup failures, post-migration path mismatches, missing binaries, unconfigured credentials, negative tool capability claims, resolved session-specific errors, or one-off task narratives.
item.degraded_mode: Without this guard, a temporary local setup failure such as a missing browser dependency can become a durable self-cited skill constraint that keeps Gormes refusing a working tool after the environment is repaired.
source_refs: ./hermes-agent/run_agent.py@e5af1dd63:_SKILL_REVIEW_PROMPT transient environment Do NOT capture section
./hermes-agent/run_agent.py@e5af1dd63:_COMBINED_REVIEW_PROMPT transient environment Do NOT capture section
ready_when: Hermes curator state transitions and run reports plus native curator prompt plumbing are complete/validated.
The slice can assert the prompt string passed to the injected CuratorReviewer; no live LLM, gateway, network, home-directory state, or tool execution is required.
The in-repo Hermes source is refreshed to 44cdf555a and includes e5af1dd63's transient-environment review prompt regression tests.
not_ready_when: The slice changes skill archive/restore/classification behavior, curator scheduling, usage scoring, or live reviewer model calls.
The prompt forbids all negative feedback instead of only forbidding durable capture of transient environment failures and unsupported tool claims.
The row is used to implement broader Skill effectiveness scoring or another learning-loop umbrella behavior.
acceptance: TestCuratorPromptTransientEnvironmentGuard fails while curatorPrompt lacks a Do NOT capture section for transient environment failures and passes after the injected CuratorReviewer receives the guard text.
The prompt tells reviewers to capture durable setup fixes under existing setup/troubleshooting skills rather than standalone negative constraints such as a tool not working.
Existing curator state/run/rename summary tests remain green.
item.note: Complete 2026-05-10: added and shipped by a bounded all-topic Hermes parity weakness sweep after refreshing Hermes to 44cdf555a and Honcho to e659b6b. Planned rows were 15, below the 90-row cap, so adding one source-backed P1 row was allowed. The sweep covered CLI/TUI, provider/auth, gateway/channels, tools, sessions/memory/Goncho, install/runtime, browser automation, docs/public surfaces, and release/operator flows. Current Codex Spark/model-catalog, Kanban slash help, stream-drop diagnostics, vision, user-story mirror, release trust, browser, install/runtime, and Goncho deltas are complete or row-backed; TD publication and broad release rows remain operator-gated or non-selectable. This row targeted the remaining learning-loop drift from Hermes e5af1dd63: background review must not turn transient environment failures into durable negative skills. TDD added a curator prompt fixture that failed on the one-line prompt, then expanded the native prompt with Do NOT capture guidance for environment-dependent failures, negative tool claims, resolved transient errors, one-off task narratives, and the positive rule to capture setup fixes instead of standalone tool-does-not-work constraints.
done_signal: Curator prompt fixtures prove Gormes preserves Hermes' transient-environment learning guard without changing curator state, archive, scheduling, or live reviewer behavior.

provenance.note: Hermes owns the class-first background-review prompt guard; Gormes ports the same durable-vs-transient boundary into the native curator prompt.

implementation: internal/skills/curator.go: curatorPrompt now includes Hermes-compatible class-level review guidance and a transient-environment Do NOT capture section.
internal/skills/curator_test.go: TestCuratorPromptTransientEnvironmentGuard captures the injected CuratorReviewer prompt and checks the durable-vs-transient boundary.
verification: RED: go test ./internal/skills -run TestCuratorPromptTransientEnvironmentGuard -count=1 failed because curatorPrompt was only the one-line native curator prompt.
GREEN: go test ./internal/skills -run TestCuratorPromptTransientEnvironmentGuard -count=1 passed after the guard text landed.

item.name: Prompt evaluation harness
item.contract: A harness that evaluates agent prompt/behavior variants against a set of test scenarios. Produces quantitative scores (task success, tool selection accuracy, response quality) for each variant. Enables data-driven prompt optimization without LLM-as-judge circularity.
ready_when: Agent loop is deterministic enough for reproducible evaluation
Test scenarios exist with known-good outcomes
not_ready_when: Agent loop is non-deterministic or cannot be replayed
acceptance: Harness runs agent with prompt variant N against M test scenarios
Produces per-scenario scores: task_success (bool), tool_accuracy (%), response_quality (1-5)
Aggregate score across all scenarios for variant comparison
Evaluation is deterministic (same variant + scenario = same score)
Harness runs <60s for 10 scenarios (fast enough for iterative optimization)
item.note: Complete: TDD expanded the prompt evaluator into a deterministic, variant-aware harness. `EvaluateVariant` runs one prompt variant against every scenario through an injected runner, records per-scenario task_success, tool_accuracy, response_quality on a 1-5 scale, error evidence, and aggregate scores, while `CompareVariants` returns deterministic aggregate ranking for prompt comparison. `DefaultPromptEvalScenarios` provides a 10-scenario local corpus covering file reads, code search, patching, tests, command safety, memory search/update, and doc refresh; focused tests prove replay determinism and sub-second execution without live LLM judging or provider calls.
done_signal: Evaluator tests prove deterministic scoring of prompt variants against known scenarios

item.name: Iterative prompt mutation and scoring loop
item.contract: Given a base prompt and evaluation harness, automatically generate prompt variants (mutations), score them, and select the best. Iterate until convergence or budget. Mutations target: tool selection heuristics, response style, task decomposition strategies.
not_ready_when: No evaluation harness to score variants
acceptance: Mutation generates N variants from base prompt
Each variant scored by evaluation harness
Best variant selected as next base for further mutation
Loop terminates when improvement < threshold or max iterations reached
Final best prompt is at least 10% better than base on aggregate score
Optimization does not require LLM API calls (uses harness scores)
item.note: Complete: TDD replaced placeholder word-deletion mutation with a deterministic GEPA-style optimizer. `GenerateVariants` creates bounded strategy mutations for exact tool selection, concrete response quality, task decomposition, and command safety. `OptimizeDetailed` scores every variant through the prompt evaluation harness, promotes the best variant as the next iteration base only when it clears the improvement threshold, records per-iteration candidates/evaluations/selected variant, and terminates with explicit converged, perfect_score, or budget_exhausted evidence. Focused tests prove N-variant generation, cumulative next-base improvement, at least 10% aggregate lift over the baseline, and convergence without LLM API calls.
done_signal: Optimizer tests prove mutation+scoring loop converges to measurably better prompt variants

item.name: Learning-loop proof demo for skills, memory, and curator
item.contract: Make the Hermes-compatible learning loop visible as an operator proof: document or demo the path from task evidence to skill creation/improvement, memory/recall persistence, curator status, and improved repeated-task behavior. The proof must use local fixtures or deterministic screenshots/output, avoid live-model hype, and link the existing skills, curator, and memory command surfaces.
item.degraded_mode: If the learning loop stays buried in architecture docs, users will believe Gormes only has the no-stack runtime wedge and will continue assigning the self-improvement story exclusively to Hermes.
ready_when: Curator state, skill surfaces, and memory docs exist and can be linked.
The builder can use deterministic local examples; no live provider, network, or Reddit/social evidence is required.
The proof can stay honest about what is shipped versus hardening.
not_ready_when: The demo claims autonomous improvement from a live model without reproducible output or fixture evidence.
The slice changes skills/curator runtime behavior instead of documenting the proof path.
The page implies every repeated task improves automatically with no operator review or trust boundary.
acceptance: Learning-loop docs show a concrete task-evidence to skill/memory/curator path with commands or deterministic sample output.
The docs distinguish skill creation, skill improvement, memory recall, and curator maintenance instead of treating learning as a single vague feature.
The landing or Why Gormes page links to the learning-loop proof without making methodology the hero.
Docs tests pin the presence of skills, memory, curator, and repeated-task proof language.
item.note: Market-positioning follow-up from 2026-05-17 gormes-planner. Hermes owns the learning-loop perception; Gormes has row-backed substrate and needs public proof.
done_signal: Learning-loop proof page is linked, deterministic, and test-guarded across skills, memory, curator, and repeated-task behavior.

provenance.note: Gormes-owned public proof row over already row-backed learning-loop substrate.
